title: Granite
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), igneous rocks, weathering (Grade 4)
notes: Coarse interlocking crystals you can see: pink and white feldspar, gray glassy quartz, black mica and hornblende. Igneous (cooled slowly underground).

title: Basalt
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), igneous rocks, volcanoes
notes: Dark gray-black, fine-grained (crystals too small to see), a few small gas holes (vesicles). Igneous (cooled quickly from lava).

title: Obsidian
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), igneous rocks, volcanoes
notes: Glossy black volcanic glass with sharp edges and conchoidal (curved, shell-like) fracture surfaces with ripple rings; strong highlights. No crystals.

title: Pumice
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), igneous rocks, density (floats on water)
notes: Pale gray-cream, rounded, full of many gas holes of different sizes (stretched a little in one direction); looks light.

title: Sandstone
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), sedimentary rocks, weathering (Grade 4)
notes: Tan-orange blocky rock, sandy speckled grains, faint horizontal layers.

title: Shale
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), sedimentary rocks, weathering (Grade 4)
notes: Dark gray, many thin flat layers seen on the edge, flaky stepped ends, a thin sheet flaking off the top.

title: Limestone with shells
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), sedimentary rocks, fossils
notes: Gray-cream fossiliferous limestone packed with ribbed shells, small snail shells and broken shell pieces.

title: Conglomerate
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), sedimentary rocks, weathering and erosion (Grade 4)
notes: Rounded pebbles of many colors and sizes (white quartz, red, gray, black, tan) cemented in a finer sandy matrix.

title: Slate
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), metamorphic rocks (shale changed by heat and pressure)
notes: Dark blue-gray thin flat slab with a smooth split face, sharp broken edges and fine splitting lines on the edge.

title: Marble
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), metamorphic rocks (limestone changed by heat and pressure), weathering by acid rain
notes: White rock with soft gray veins and a sugary mosaic of small crystals with sparkles.

title: Gneiss
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), metamorphic rocks (foliation from pressure)
notes: Bold wavy alternating light (white, pink) and dark bands (foliation), each band speckled with mineral grains.

title: Quartzite
use: Rock-cycle cards (Grade 6 rock cycle), metamorphic rocks (sandstone changed by heat and pressure)
notes: Pale pink and white, glassy-granular mosaic of fused sand grains, massive with no layers, glassy highlights. Drawn from general knowledge of quartzite; no reference page was used.

title: Rock layers in a canyon wall
use: RockLayers picture (older layers at the bottom), sedimentary rocks, fossils and Earth history
notes: Canyon wall with nine horizontal sedimentary layers of different colors, thicknesses and textures (cream limestone on top, pale cross-bedded sandstone, red layers, gray, green-gray shale, brown sandstone at the bottom); the wall steps down to the right; sky, clouds, shrubs, a hazy far wall. Older layers are lower.

title: Fish fossil
notes: Whole herring-like fish skeleton (like Knightia) pressed into a pale limestone slab: skull with eye socket and gill cover, backbone of vertebrae, ribs, fins with rays, forked tail.

title: Shell fossils
notes: Ribbed brachiopod shells (fan-shaped, with a beak and growth lines) and a coiled ammonite in a gray-tan rock with broken shell bits.
